source.anchor_kjv: My strength is dried up like a potsherd; and my tongue cleaveth to my jaws; and thou hast brought me into the dust of death. ... I thirst.
source.thread: Psalm 22:15 paints the killing thirst of a dying man -- strength dried up like a potsherd, tongue cleaving to the jaws, sinking into the dust of death -- written in the first person by David about someone else's death, about 1000 years before Jesus cried 'I thirst' on the cross (John 19:28). This is a DESCRIPTIVE match -- the psalm pictures the thirst behind that cry, it does NOT foretell or cite it (John 19:28's fulfilment formula is referred to Psalm 69:21, which is never quoted here). The gospel turn: the One who made every river and offers the world living water hung there with nothing, thirsting in your place, so you could drink and never thirst again -- and that water is Himself.

source.hook_line: The One who made every ocean gasped two words on a cross: I thirst.
source.spoken_script: The One who made every ocean gasped two words on a cross: I thirst. Psalm twenty-two. David wrote it in the first person, but he was picturing someone else's death. Watch the body give out: "My strength is dried up like a potsherd; and my tongue cleaveth to my jaws; and thou hast brought me into the dust of death." Dried clay; a tongue stuck fast; a man sinking into the dust of death. Then John records the dying Jesus' cry: "I thirst." Psalm twenty-two doesn't foretell that cry — it paints the thirst behind it, a thousand years before He felt it. And think who is thirsting: the One who made every river and spring, who offers the world living water — hanging there with nothing, in your place. He went dry so that you could drink and never thirst again. The God who made every ocean cried out in thirst — so He could hand you the one water that never fails. And that water is Himself.

platforms.label: YouTube (Long-form 16:9)
platforms.title: Psalm 22 Painted the Thirst Behind the Cross - 1,000 Years Before Jesus Felt It
platforms.description:
On the cross, Jesus gasped two words: I thirst. Before we get to John 19, Psalm 22 has already painted the body that would say it.

Psalm 22:15 (KJV): "My strength is dried up like a potsherd; and my tongue cleaveth to my jaws; and thou hast brought me into the dust of death."

David wrote this in the first person, about a dying man he was not. Strength gone like dried clay. Tongue fused to the jaw. The body sinking into the dust of death. A thousand years before Jesus hung on the cross.

Psalm 22 does not formally predict or cite the cry - it paints the physical reality behind it, a thousand years early. That's a different kind of foreknowledge, and it is no less striking.

And think who is thirsting. The One who made every river, every ocean, every spring of water - who told a Samaritan woman He was the living water she was looking for - hung there with nothing, in your place. He went dry so you could drink and never thirst again. That water is Himself.

Psalm 22 | John 19 | KJV
